How much does carpet installation cost on Whidbey Island, WA?

Figure $4 to $7 per square foot installed on Whidbey Island — the carpet, the pad, labor, new tack strip and haul-away all inside that number. Most island projects land between $2,000 and $4,500, and a 1,200 sq ft main floor with a staircase typically runs $5,500 to $8,500. Grade drives the price more than anything, and you set it yourself from samples spread out in your own rooms.
Does the mobile carpet showroom really come out to Whidbey Island?

It does. The van rides the Mukilteo ferry into Clinton — or comes down through Deception Pass for the north end — carrying 20+ carpet samples and all three pad grades. We lay samples on the exact floors they would cover, measure every room and stair, and leave a written price before catching the boat back. The visit is free, and you never leave the island.
What does it cost to stretch carpet on Whidbey Island?

Stretching starts at $99 per room on Whidbey Island. A power stretcher pulls ripples, waves and trip hazards flat for roughly a fifth of what new carpet costs — the right call for a cabin or rental where the pile still stands and the color still works. Loose carpet is common in older beach houses, so it's worth checking before you price a replacement.
What do carpeted stairs cost on Whidbey Island?

Stair installation starts at $18 per step, done waterfall or cap-and-band. Landings and pie-shaped winders — common in the island's split-entry and view homes — are measured and written into the quote at the visit, so the number you approve is the number you pay.
How long does carpet installation take on Whidbey Island?

Most Whidbey Island homes are carpeted in one day, and we plan the ferry crossing so the crew lands early. Three or four rooms plus a staircase is a standard day's work; a big house with stairs and heavy furniture can run into a second. Your quote spells out the schedule in writing.
Do the installers move furniture, or do I arrange that?

We move it. Beds, dressers, couches and tables are included on most island jobs, and everything goes back where it stood. You take care of the small things — closet floors, electronics, breakables, and anything you'd rather box up yourself before the crew arrives.
Is it better to restretch carpet or replace it?

Restretch when the pile still stands, the backing is sound and the color still suits the room — a $99-per-room fix instead of a whole new floor. Replace when traffic lanes are matted flat, seams are letting go, the backing is crumbling, or pet odor has outlived a professional cleaning. We tell you which situation you have before any quote is written.
Which Whidbey Island communities do you serve?

All of them — Clinton, Langley, Freeland, Greenbank, Coupeville and Oak Harbor, plus the beach communities between them: Maxwelton, Scatchet Head, Sandy Hook, Possession Shores, Mutiny Bay, Bush Point, Lagoon Point, Admirals Cove, Bayview and out to Penn Cove. If a county road or a gravel drive reaches your door, the van does too.
What's the best carpet for pets in a Whidbey Island home?

Solution-dyed nylon with a sealed backing over a moisture-barrier pad. The barrier keeps accidents and wet-dog drips out of the subfloor — the source of permanent odor — and solution-dyed fiber stands up to a diluted-bleach cleaning without fading. For a house where sandy paws come straight in off Double Bluff, it's the practical choice. The barrier pad upgrade starts at $0.65 per square foot.
What warranty comes with a Whidbey Island carpet installation?

Every installation carries OC Flooring's 1-year workmanship warranty, plus the mill's own warranty on the carpet — usually 10 to 25 years on wear and stain depending on grade. Both are spelled out on your written quote. Since the pad you choose can affect the mill's coverage, all three pad grades come along on the visit so you decide with the facts in front of you.
